subject: Request: premium surcharge waiver + packaging structure for CardioNova (exec sign-off)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Victor Chen <victor.chen@cardionova.com>, CardioNova Sales Ops <sales.ops@cardionova.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Premium surcharge waiver + packaging structure for CardioNova (exec sign-off)

Team —

Quick summary up front: CardioNova is asking us to waive the 15% multi-region "premium surcharge" for their Dedicated + Private hybrid deployment. They are a strategic prospect (potential $1.1M ARR in year 1, $2.9M ARR by year 2 under the proposed ramp) and the ask is tied to a three-region private connector and a 12-month minimum commit.

Why this matters now:
- They’ve received competitive pressure from two vendors who will absorb the surcharge for the first six months.
- CardioNova needs predictable latency across EU/US regions & a private instance in our APAC partner region during the pilot.
- Loss risk: without concession they may push the pilot to a competitor next week.

What we propose (attached: proposal_cardionova_v3.pdf and redwood_margin_model_Q2.xlsx):
- Waive the 15% premium surcharge for the first 6 months of their 12-month commit, then revert to standard surcharge after month 6.
- Tie the waiver to a renewal trigger: if they convert to a 24-month contract at month 10, the surcharge remains waived for the remaining term.
- Require a non-refundable onboarding fee of $25k to offset ramp.

Financial impact (high level):
- Estimated one-time margin hit in Y1: ~$96k (see model).
- NPV of deal at discounted rate (internal model): positive vs. losing the account to competitor.

Why I’m escalating: this exceeds Marissa’s $50k discretionary concession band and materially changes surcharge policy precedent. I’m requesting explicit VP / CFO sign-off to proceed.

Requested approval ask: 
- VP/CFO sign-off to approve 6-month waiver per the structure above, with the onboarding fee and renewal trigger conditions.

Can I get a quick read from Marissa and Kimberly on whether the onboarding fee + renewal trigger is sufficient mitigation? If yes, I’ll prep an executive memo and submit to Finance for sign-off.

Thanks — Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): proposal_cardionova_v3.pdf (18 pages), redwood_margin_model_Q2.xlsx (workbook)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Premium surcharge waiver + packaging structure for CardioNova (exec sign-off)

Rachel —

Thanks for the clear write-up and attachments. I’m sympathetic to the churn risk here, and I agree the onboarding fee + renewal trigger are good mitigations. A few clarifying items before we take to execs: 

1) Can you confirm the 12-month commit baseline and the explicit ARR math if they exercise the 24-month renewal at month 10? I want the sensitivity (best / base / downside) in one slide.
2) Does the ask include dedicated support SLAs or SRE hours? If yes we need to price those into the model separately.
3) If we cap the waiver at 6 months, are there operational exceptions we need to document (e.g., region-by-region cutover windows)?

Operational note: I can approve up to $50k in equivalent concessions. This looks north of that, so we will need VP/CFO sign-off for the margin hit. I think Finance will be open to the onboarding fee plus a hard renewal condition (makes it easier to justify).

If you can send me a one-slide sensitivity and confirm support hours by EOD Tues I’ll draft the memo and route to Chris (VP Sales) + Markus (Finance) for expedited review.

Subject: Re: Premium surcharge waiver + packaging structure for CardioNova (exec sign-off)

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple points from our side: 

- We are prepared to sign a 12-mo minimum commit and provide a letter of intent for the 24-mo conversion if the initial pilot meets performance criteria.
- Our preference would be a full surcharge waiver for the first 6 months rather than a partial rebate; operationally that is simpler for us.
- We will pay the $25k onboarding fee but would like the onboarding to include a one-week on-site integration support window at our San Mateo office (we’ll cover travel costs).

If Redwood can confirm the waiver structure + include the on-site week in the onboarding package I believe we can execute by May 10 and start the pilot the week of May 17.

Best —
Victor Chen

Subject: Executive memo: premium surcharge waiver request for CardioNova — formal sign-off requested

Chris/Markus —

Per Marissa’s guidance and CardioNova’s confirmation, I’m escalating with a formal recommendation and ask for exec sign-off. Key facts: 

- Account: CardioNova Health (prospect -> strategic customer)
- Deal id: RWF-2345
- Proposed commercial structure: 12-month minimum commit; 6-month full premium surcharge waiver; $25k onboarding fee; one-week on-site integration during onboarding; renewal-trigger to retain waiver if they sign/convert to 24 months by month 10.
- Financial impact: estimated $96k margin reduction in Y1 vs base list; NPV positive when accounting for retention & strategic value (see attached model).
- Risk mitigations: onboarding fee, renewal trigger, limited on-site week (customer covers travel), and a post-pilot performance SLO review at month 5.

Recommendation: Authorize the 6-month surcharge waiver under the above conditions. This requires one of you (VP Sales or CFO) to sign off so we can send DocuSign and lock the pilot start date (target week of May 17).

Attachments: proposal_cardionova_v3.pdf, redwood_margin_model_Q2.xlsx
DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/placeholder/ABC-9876

If you approve, please reply with: 
- "APPROVED — Markus" or "APPROVED — Chris" (or provide edits).

Thanks for the quick read — this is time-sensitive; Victor wants an answer before EOD Monday.

— Rachel
